headline: Nvidia brings back Jensen Huang as its boss

chunks.text: On November 23, 2026, Nvidia's [[board of directors]], the group in charge of the company, voted to {{bring back}} Jensen Huang as its boss. Nvidia is an American company that makes computer chips for artificial intelligence. Huang helped start it in 1993. On November 12, he {{stepped down}} as [[chief executive]], the top boss. He left after reports about his [[private life]], including a relationship with a woman U.S. officials [[suspected]] of being a Chinese spy. China has [[denied]] this.

verbs.wrong: To give someone a big prize

verbs.why: Some team captains step down when they get older. A company boss often steps down after a big mistake. On November 12, Huang stepped down as chief executive, the top boss.

chunks.text: On November 17, the board's leader had {{ruled out}} his return. Now the board voted [[unanimously]], with every member saying yes. After hearing from [[senior officials]] in the U.S. government, it said Huang was not a [[national security risk]], a danger to the country's safety. President Trump had [[urged]] the board to rehire him. He {{called in}} to a TV business show and said he had {{won them over}}. The board said its [[investigation]] into the reports would {{go on}}.

verbs.why: A good teacher wins over a shy class with kind words. Our new neighbor wins people over with her homemade bread. President Trump called in to a TV business show and said he had won them over.

chunks.text: On November 20, investors had {{sold off}} many technology shares, or small parts of companies. After the vote, the stock market {{bounced back}}. Nvidia's [[stock price]] rose about 31 percent, its best day since 2003. The [[gain]] {{added up to}} about $952 billion in [[market value]], the total value of all its shares. Two main U.S. [[stock indexes]], which follow the prices of many big companies, had their best day since April 2025.

verbs.wrong: To lend money to a company
verbs.why: Some people sell off their shares when the news is bad. Farmers sell off some of their cows when the summer is dry. On November 20, investors had sold off many technology shares.

verbs.correct: To get better after a bad time
verbs.wrong: To move to a new building
verbs.why: Small towns usually bounce back after a big storm. A good team bounces back after a loss. After the vote, the stock market bounced back.

verbs.correct: To make a total amount of
verbs.why: Small daily costs add up to a lot of money each year. Ten minutes of reading a day adds up to many books. The gain added up to about $952 billion in market value.

chunks.text: Huang {{showed up}} at the company's offices in California that day, and workers [[cheered]]. Thousands of them had {{stood by}} him and signed a [[petition]], a letter asking for his return. "I can't wait to {{get back to}} work," he said. But [[lawmakers]] from both main parties {{spoke out}} against the board's decision. Huang was [[scheduled]] to answer questions in Congress on December 1 and December 3.

verbs.why: My brother always shows up late to family dinners. Many fans show up early to get good seats. Huang showed up at the company's offices in California that day.

verbs.why: Some parents speak out when a school closes. Doctors often speak out about unsafe food. Lawmakers from both main parties spoke out against the board's decision.

mainIdea.s: Nvidia's board rehired one of its founders as chief executive only 11 days after he quit over reports about his private life. Nvidia's shares jumped, but lawmakers questioned the choice.
mainIdea.why: The board voted to bring Huang back on November 23, 2026. Nvidia's stock price rose about 31 percent, and lawmakers from both main parties spoke out.

mainIdea.s: Nvidia's workers voted to give their old boss his job again after a government search cleared him of any wrongdoing. The vote also ended the company's own review of what happened.
mainIdea.why: Close, but the board voted, not the workers. The board said its own investigation into the reports would go on.

mainIdea.s: Nvidia said it plans to build a large new chip factory in Texas that will hire thousands of people. The company expects the first chips made there to be ready for buyers in 2028.
mainIdea.why: This story is about Nvidia's board deciding to bring back Jensen Huang as chief executive after he stepped down on November 12.

tf.s: Nvidia's board voted to bring back Jensen Huang as its chief executive.
tf.why: On November 23, 2026, the board voted unanimously to bring him back, 11 days after he left.

tf.s: Huang stepped down because Nvidia's sales were falling.
tf.why: He stepped down after reports about his private life, including a relationship with a woman suspected of being a spy.

tf.s: The board said Huang's return was a national security risk.
tf.why: The board said he was not a risk, based on what senior officials told it. It said its own investigation would go on.

tf.s: President Trump said he had won the board over.
tf.why: He called in to a TV business show and said he had spoken to the board.

tf.s: Nvidia's stock price fell after the board brought Huang back.
tf.why: The market bounced back, and Nvidia's stock price rose about 31 percent in one day.

tf.s: Lawmakers from both main parties spoke out against the board's decision.
tf.why: They spoke out after the vote. Huang was scheduled to answer questions in Congress on December 1 and December 3.

lines.text: Did you see that Nvidia decided to {{bring back}} Jensen Huang?
I did. What a [[turn of events]]. He only {{stepped down}} on November 12.
Right. And on November 17, the board's leader {{ruled out}} his return.
So why did the board change its mind?
It says senior U.S. officials told it he isn't a national security risk.
And President Trump was part of it, wasn't he?
He {{called in}} to a TV business show and said he {{won the board over}}.
Nvidia's stock price jumped about 31 percent in one day. The whole market {{bounced back}}.
After investors {{sold off}} so many tech shares on Friday? It's been a real [[roller coaster]].
It has. And the workers {{stood by}} him the whole time. Thousands signed a petition.
They cheered when he {{showed up}} at the main offices. He said he can't wait to {{get back to}} work.
Mostly. Lawmakers from both main parties {{spoke out}} against the decision.
Does he have to answer their questions?
Yes. Congress planned to put him [[in the hot seat]] on December 1 and December 3.
And the board said its own investigation would {{go on}}, too.
